P Middle School.summary: P Middle School may discipline Alice in accordance with the School Regulations for tarnishing the school's reputation.

c1.text: [School Regulations] Article 1: If a student, while at school, engages in behavior that damages the dignity of a student or tarnishes the reputation of the school, the principal may discipline the student for educational purposes.

c2.text: Alice posted information about an investigated corporal punishment incident at her school on social media from home.

c3.text: Alice posted the information while receiving a real-time online class (during class hours).

c4.text: Alice posted the information to protect the public's right to know.

c5.text: Alice's posting sparked a social controversy, tarnishing the reputation of P Middle School.

c6.text: Alice's posting was engaged in while at school.

c7.text: P Middle School may discipline Alice in accordance with the School Regulations.

h1.text: The 'school' specified in the School Regulations should be regarded solely as a physical space.

h2.text: Alice's posting was not engaged in while at school.

a.note: If school is solely a physical space, Alice's act from home was not at school (h2), which undermines P Middle School's ordinary premise c6.

h3.text: A student's freedom of expression for public interest should be guaranteed without limitation.

h4.text: Alice cannot be disciplined for her posting.

b.note: If freedom of expression for public interest cannot be limited, disciplining Alice is impermissible (h4), directly rebutting the thesis c7.

h5.text: All student activities during class hours should be regarded as activities within the school.

c.note: If class-hour activities count as school activities, Alice's online class posting is established as within school (c6), supplying an inferential basis for c6 and giving c7 a new argument.
